title: Copeland Septet group of galaxies
caption: The Copeland Septet galaxy group, imaged for the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys (Kitt Peak and Cerro Tololo)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This view shows a group of galaxies known by the nickname the Copeland Septet, in the constellation Leo. Galaxy groups are small collections of galaxies held together by their mutual gravity, and their members can interact and disturb one another over time.

The image comes from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Astronomers combined pictures taken at Kitt Peak National Observatory and at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory to assemble what was described as the largest map of the sky ever made, holding more than a billion galaxies.

That map, released in its final form, set the stage for a 5-year survey by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). That project aims to shed new light on the nature of dark energy. Dark energy is the name astronomers give to whatever is causing the expansion of the Universe to speed up, and what it really is remains a major open question. Mapping the positions of huge numbers of galaxies is one way to trace how that expansion has changed.
